text_pillars.excerpt:
# Style bible

- Look: rendered 3D game asset (toon / cel-shaded), like a model in the game engine, not a flat 2D drawing
- Chunky toy-like proportions with soft rounded edges, like vinyl collectible toys
- Candy pastel base colors with neon magenta and cyan accents
- Single subject centered on a plain background
- 3/4 front view, soft studio lighting
- Game-ready, under 15k triangles

assets.title: Key art
assets.prompt: Key art for the game Pocket Kaiju: Mochi, the small round pastel-pink kaiju from the reference image, mid-stomp in the middle of a glowing neon miniature Tokyo at night built on a tabletop, tiny tin-toy robots tumbling away, a rainbow atomic breath beam lighting the scene, candy pastel buildings with neon magenta and cyan signs, cinematic low angle, toy-like 3D render with soft depth of field

assets.title: Tin Brute
assets.prompt: A chunky tin toy robot brute with a big boxy tin body, thick stubby legs, a square head with a single round visor eye and two large clamp hands, painted blue and grey with rivets and a slightly dented chest plate

assets.title: Tin Scout
assets.prompt: A small wind-up tin toy robot with a round tin body, two stubby antenna with bobbing ball tips, a key on its back and a single round visor eye, arms that stick out stiffly, painted with a red and cream tin finish

assets.title: Tin Titan
assets.prompt: A giant wind-up tin toy mech, three times the height of a small kaiju, with a chunky cylinder body, a large wind-up key on its back, a single round searchlight eye on the front of the head, and two stubby cannon arms; painted cream and red tin with neon trim along the seams

assets.title: Mochi
assets.prompt: A pocket-sized pastel kaiju named Mochi with a round soft pale pink body, stubby arms, a short wagging tail with a small pastel tip, a tiny crest of soft cream spikes on the head and large friendly eyes with glossy highlights, standing on two chunky feet

assets.title: Neon block
assets.prompt: A miniature city block on a tabletop with three small toy-scale towers, glowing neon signs in magenta and cyan, a striped awning shop, a small tram track with a rounded tram and a few round street trees on a flat pastel base

assets.title: Paper lantern
assets.prompt: A round paper lantern on a thin wire, pastel pink and cream with a soft glow inside and a small tassel at the bottom

assets.title: Vending machine
assets.prompt: A chunky toy-scale vending machine with a rounded pastel body, a glowing front panel with a few colourful product rows, a coin slot and a small tray at the bottom, standing on four short feet

assets.title: Perk card
assets.prompt: A rounded trading card with a pastel frame, a large round icon in the center, a small ribbon banner across the top and a glowing cyan edge, empty of text

assets.title: Mochi Roar
assets.prompt: A cute small kaiju roar: a high-pitched, squeaky, rumbling growl that rises into a playful chirpy yip, soft and bubbly like a toy creature, not scary or deep

assets.title: Stomp Impact
assets.prompt: A heavy, chunky stomp impact: a soft thud with a squashy rubber-toy bounce, a low sub-bass punch, a short cardboard-like crunch on top, and a small puff of air, dry and punchy with no reverb tail

assets.title: Tin Robot Pop
assets.prompt: A tin toy robot popping apart: a metallic clatter and ringing tin rattle, a springy boing, a few small bolts and gears spinning off, and a bright cheerful pop at the end, playful and slightly comical

assets.title: Arcade Synthwave Loop
assets.prompt: An upbeat 30-second arcade synthwave loop at about 128 BPM: punchy bouncy synth bass, bright analog lead melody, driving four-on-the-floor drums, shimmering arpeggios and a retro video game energy, seamless loop that restarts cleanly

assets.title: Coin Pickup
assets.prompt: A bright coin pickup jingle: two or three quick rising chime notes on a glockenspiel or bell tone, a little sparkle at the end, cheerful and short, arcade-style

assets.title: Announcer: KAIJU TIME!
assets.prompt: KAIJU TIME!

assets.title: Rainbow Breath Beam
assets.prompt: A horizontally tileable looping energy beam texture: a bright pastel rainbow core band runs along the full length, with neon magenta and neon cyan glowing edges on both sides, soft light falloff, flat seamless left and right ends, transparent surroundings

# Core loop

1. Spawn on a neon block of the miniature city.
2. Waves of tin-toy invaders march in from the edges.
3. Stomp invaders, tail-whip groups, charge the rainbow atomic breath.
4. Smash props for coins, health and perk tokens.
5. Clear the wave to unlock the next district, or fall and start over.

- Hits should be juicy: hit-stop, squash and stretch, sparkle bursts.
- Every prop should feel like a chunky toy that gives way when hit.
- Runs stay short: a full run ends in about 3 minutes.

body.content:
# Design

How the game plays: the loop, the roguelike run and the combat rules that tie the rest together.

Runs last about 3 minutes. Each run is a wave-based defence of the neon city, and every smashed prop and defeated invader feeds into the perks you pick.

# Roguelike run structure

- A run is 3 waves across 3 districts, then a boss invader.
- After each wave the player picks one perk card from three options.
- Perks stack: tail-whip reach, stomp shockwave, breath colour bands, extra hearts.
- A failed run keeps coins and unlocks one new perk for the pool.
- Seeds are shown on the result screen so runs can be shared.

# Invaders

The tin-toy robot invaders. They are clumsy, wind-up and slightly unfair in numbers, never in damage.

Groups by role: small scouts that swarm, heavier brutes that block and charge.

# Pocket Kaiju

A bite-sized 3D arcade brawler where you play Mochi, a pocket-sized pastel kaiju, defending a neon miniature Tokyo from waves of clumsy tin-toy robot invaders.

## Core loop

- Short 3-minute roguelike runs through a tabletop neon city.
- Stomp, tail-whip and charge a rainbow atomic breath.
- Smash chunky toy-like props for coins, health and temporary perks.
- Each run ends with a perk-shaped build that changes the next run.

## Cast

| **Mochi**: the hero, all stomp and sparkle | **Tin Scout**: swarms in packs of six to ten | **Tin Brute**: shields the scouts, then charges | **Tin Titan**: the minute-three boss |

## Look

Rendered 3D toy style: chunky vinyl-collectible proportions, candy pastels with neon magenta and cyan. Mochi's art is the project pillar, so every new image matches it. See `pillars/style-bible.md`.

models.license: FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License · images may be used commercially, the model only non-commercially

models.label: BiRefNet
models.blurb: A proper AI cut-out: hair, holes and soft edges come out clean. The same model ElevenLabs uses.

deps.label: PyTorch
deps.blurb: Runs AI models on your graphics card. Brings its own Python, so nothing on your system changes.

deps.label: Image libraries
deps.blurb: Diffusers and Transformers, which every image model here is built on.

deps.label: Cut-out add-ons
deps.blurb: torchvision, timm, kornia and einops, which BiRefNet needs.

idea.label: Idea
idea.blurb: Say what you want in your own words.
idea.help: Write one thing, the way you would describe it to an artist. “A grumpy frog knight in rusty armour” works better than one word.

fields.label: What do you want to make?
fields.placeholder: A grumpy frog knight in rusty armour

list.label: List of ideas
list.blurb: One idea per line. Every step after it runs for each line.
list.help: Great for sets: ten potions, five enemies. Add a line later and only the new one is made.

fields.label: One idea per line
fields.placeholder:
Red health potion
Blue mana potion
Green poison flask

my_picture.label: My picture
my_picture.blurb: Use a picture from your computer or this project.
my_picture.help: Drop a picture on this card, paste one, or pick one you already made in Tessera. Nothing is sent anywhere until a later step uses it.

my_model.label: My 3D model
my_model.blurb: Use a 3D model from your computer or this project.
my_model.help: Works with .glb files. Use it to add a skeleton or animations to a model you already have.

style.label: Art style
style.blurb: One look shared by every picture you connect it to.
style.help: Connect one Art style to several picture steps and everything matches. Your project's own style is always followed as well.

choices.label: Hand-Painted Fantasy
choices.hint: Warm painterly brushstrokes, sculpted bevels, readable silhouettes, soft rim light.

choices.label: Low-Poly Isometric
choices.hint: Crisp faceted geometry, clean gradients, diorama-ready 3/4 isometric proportions.

choices.label: PS1 32-Bit Retro
choices.hint: Low-poly affine texture feel, crunchy dithered color palette, nostalgic 1998 aesthetic.

choices.label: Anime Cel-Shaded
choices.hint: Bold ink outlines, two-tone cel shadows, expressive graphic highlights.

choices.label: Clean UI Inventory Icon
choices.hint: High-contrast centered item icon, bold outer contour, readable at 64px.

vary.label: Make versions
vary.blurb: Turns one idea into several: red, blue, golden…
vary.help: Every line is added to the idea. “Dragon” with the lines “fire”, “ice” and “poison” gives three dragons.

fields.label: One version per line
fields.placeholder:
made of fire
made of ice
made of poison

draw.label: Draw a picture
draw.blurb: An AI artist draws your idea.
draw.help: Tessera picks the AI model, the shape and the background for you; change any of them if you like. If 3D comes next, it also asks for a full view and a neutral pose, so the model turns out well.

fields.label: What should it show?
fields.placeholder: A grumpy frog knight in rusty armour

pixel.label: Draw pixel art
pixel.blurb: A real pixel sprite: exact size, limited colours.
pixel.help: Pixel Studio's own engine: drawn for the grid, then locked to it. Saved sprites open in Pixel Studio.

fields.label: What should it show?
fields.placeholder: A slime with a tiny crown

pick.label: Let me choose
pick.blurb: Stops so you can pick your favourite.
pick.help: The steps after this wait for you. Click the picture you like and they carry on. With a list, you choose one for each idea.

change.label: Change a picture
change.blurb: Describe an edit: “give it a red cape”.
change.help: The rest of the picture stays the same. Ask for one or two changes at a time.

views.label: Draw its other sides
views.blurb: Draws the left side and the back of the same thing.
views.help: Connect it to “Other sides” on Make it 3D and the back of the model is drawn instead of guessed.

cutout.label: Remove background
cutout.blurb: Keeps the subject, clears everything behind it.
cutout.help: Made on your computer, free. Works best on plain backgrounds; with BiRefNet installed (Settings → This PC) it handles busy ones too.

recolor.label: Recolour
recolor.blurb: The same picture in other colours.
recolor.help: Made on your computer, free. Handy for team colours, rarity tiers and enemy types.

icons.label: Make icons
icons.blurb: Square, see-through icons, all framed the same way.
icons.help: Made on your computer, free. Ready for inventories and menus.

split.label: Cut into pieces
split.blurb: Finds every object on a sheet and cuts each one out.
split.help: Made on your computer, free. Best with objects spaced apart on a plain background.

tile.label: Make it repeat
tile.blurb: A seamless texture for floors and walls.
tile.help: Made on your computer, free: the colour plus the maps a game engine uses for light (normal, roughness, height).

make3d.label: Make it 3D
make3d.blurb: Turns a picture into a textured 3D model.
make3d.help: Takes a few minutes. Best with one subject, fully in view, on a plain background.

rig.label: Add a skeleton
rig.blurb: Gives a character bones so it can move.
rig.help: Works on characters with arms and legs, standing with a little space under the arms. Objects and vehicles don't need one.

animate.label: Make it move
animate.help: Pick as many moves as you like. They land in one file, ready for your game, and come from whoever made the skeleton. Fine-tune them later in Motion Studio.

sound.label: Make a sound
sound.blurb: Effects, music or a spoken line.
sound.help: Describe the sound (“heavy wooden door creaks open”). For a voice, write exactly what should be said. Length and looping are worked out from your words.

fields.label: What should it sound like?
fields.placeholder: A heavy wooden door creaks open

save.label: Save to project
save.blurb: Puts the results in your project as assets.
save.help: Connect anything you want to keep. Pictures, models, animations and sounds of the same thing land on one asset page, and your game's coding agent sees them.

note.label: Note
note.blurb: A reminder to yourself. Does nothing.
note.help: For leaving yourself or your team a hint.
